First, we recall the following identities: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }
$$

Next, we expand the parentheses and use the above identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{csc}^{2}⁡\theta ({tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) & ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{csc}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot {sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}\cdot \frac{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-\frac{1}{\cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }}\cdot \cancel{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }-1 \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall the different forms of the secant-tangent Identity:

$$
\begin{aligned} & (1) & 1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & (2) & {tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 \\  & (3) & {sec}^{2}⁡\theta -{tan}^{2}⁡\theta =1\end{aligned}
$$

We can rewrite our expression using $(2),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sec}^{2}⁡\theta -1 & ={tan}^{2}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{csc}^{2}⁡\theta ({tan}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )={tan}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$
